candidate.answerReason: The five odd-score games must be the five losses. Their opponents scored 30 runs in those games and 15 runs in the even-score games, totaling 45.

methods.label: Use odd scores to identify the losses
methods.explanation:
Runs are whole numbers, so whenever the team scored twice its opponent's score, the team's score had to be even. Therefore each of the five odd-score games, with scores \(1,3,5,7,9\), must have been a loss. Since there were exactly five losses, these are all the losses, and the five even-score games are the other games.

In each loss, the opponent scored one more run. Those opponent scores were \(2,4,6,8,10\), totaling \(30\). In the other games, the opponent scored half the team's score, giving \(1,2,3,4,5\), totaling \(15\).

Every game belongs to exactly one of these two groups, so the opponents' total was
\[
30+15=\boxed{45}
\]
runs, choice C.
methods.levelReason: Uses the whole-number nature of scores, odd and even numbers, and elementary arithmetic.

candidate.annotationRationale: Parity is the decisive target: a score twice another integer must be even. The exact count of five losses then forces the assignment of every game. Understanding the twice-as-many relationship and computing the two totals support the method.
